h: לְרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ מְנַחֵם אָב, ד׳ Rosh Chodesh Menachem Av, 4
"In the Light of the King's Countenance Is Life": Tes, Hearing and Swallowing

p: "He made the letter Tes king over hearing," and so on,
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קנב, א)
טֵי״ת נְהִירוּ דְּחַיִּין בְּכָל אֲתַר וְכוּלֵּי.
Tes is the light of life in every place," and so on.
And this is what is written (Mishlei 16:15):
"In the light of the King's countenance is life."
which is called "the light, that it was good";
and the letter Tes indicates this,
for the first Tes in the Torah
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
"And Elokim saw the light, that it was good"
and it is the primordial light
that was hidden away in the Torah.
And this month is the time
in that they did not listen to the words of the Nevi'im.
they will be able to merit eternal life,
to "the light of the King's countenance," which is life.
And the rectification is through the attribute
"'Good' means none other than a tzaddik,
'Say of the tzaddik that he is good'"
וְגַם עַל זֶה מוֹרֶה אוֹת ט׳.
and the letter Tes indicates this as well.
And it says "the letter Tes over hearing"
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רל, א)
"'Those who fear Elokim' — from the side of Yitzchak,
'Hashem, I have heard Your report and I was afraid.'"
And this is as it says (Yeshayah 55:3):
when it is as it should be,
and the heart indicates fear of Heaven,
עַל מִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם.
as referring to one who has no fear of Heaven.
into the depths of the heart,
"Then you will understand the fear of Hashem."
And this is the side of Yitzchak,
as stated in the holy Zohar

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 152a, Terumah — “Come and see: Tes is the illumination of life in every place. Therefore the verse begins with it in 'that it was good,' as it is written: 'God saw the light, that it was good.' From this letter the destroying angel flees—or rather, he is not given permission to enter there. This letter differs from kuf: kuf is not established in any settled place in the world; its sign is 'A man of evil speech shall not be established in the land.' Tes is established in every place and is properly fitted to settle there; wherever tes is, kuf has no settled place. ... Just as this letter rules in this place, so another letter rules in the place of Gehinnom. Which is it? Qof.” The source contrasts tes with kuf in the account of a place protected from death. The retrieved text also preserves a variant reading of ches for kuf. Rav Tzadok's argument follows the kuf reading quoted in his manuscript.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, Pinchas (Ra'aya Meheimna) — "'Men of valor, God-fearing, men of truth' (Shemos 18:21): 'men of valor' — from the side of the right of Avraham, where there is the seeing of Torah; 'God-fearing' — from the side of Yitzchak, where there is hearing, as Chavakuk the prophet said, 'Hashem, I have heard Your report and I was afraid' (Chavakuk 3:2); 'men of truth' — from the side of Yaakov, where there is smell."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Tammuz and Av 1:7 — “The breaking among the primordial kings was in the aspect of the eyes, and in the aspect of the ear there is repair and life, in the secret of ‘Listen, and your soul shall live’ (Yeshayahu 55:3). Therefore, when the month came that is in the aspect of hearing, as was said, repair came about for the aspect of sight; therefore in it the mountaintops were seen.” Connection: Bnei Yissaschar too makes the hearing of Av the repair of the failure of sight, the movement Rav Tzadok traces from Tammuz to Av.

Woe to those Torah scholars who engage in Torah and have no fear of Heaven”: on Proverbs 17:16 (“a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, and he has no heart”) — the “heart” lacking is fear of Heaven.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

p: And the version of the Geonim
"He made the letter Tes king over swallowing."
and therefore over the Luz bone,
over which the letter Tes rules,
as stated in the holy Zohar
And over this month He made the letter Tes king,
that is, to rectify everything completely,
so that there will no longer be any dominion
And this can come about only
when one rectifies the entire blemish of the serpent,
And this is why it says "swallowing":
that the swallowing should be in holiness;
Rosh Chodesh Av falls on Shabbos;
for regarding Shabbos it is brought from the Arizal
that even when one eats a hearty meal
that is, for the sake of Heaven,
the body's pleasure too is in holiness.
and it is from the side of the Tree of Life:

inlineHeadings.text: Rosh Chodesh Av on Shabbos: rectifying eating

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Shevat 4 — “And the Arizal's version: ‘He made the letter tzaddi king over swallowing (le'itah), and Shevat in the year, and the gizzard in the soul,’ according to what it says (Berachos 61b), ‘the gizzard grinds’; that is, to repair…” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other treatment of “swallowing” in Sefer Yetzirah, here for Shevat; the two versions give swallowing to Av and to Shevat.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 118a — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosi: Whoever delights the Shabbos is given an inheritance without boundaries, as it says, 'Then you shall delight in Hashem, and I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth, and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father' (Yeshayahu 58:14)." Rashi: without boundaries — that has no end.
